chapter_title: Banks and the Magic of Finance

questions.question: What is the apex central bank responsible for supervising commercial banks and issuing currency notes in India?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central monetary authority that regulates commercial banks, manages currency supply, and sets financial safety rules.

questions.question: Which mobile digital payment system developed by NPCI allows instant 24/7 bank-to-bank transactions via QR codes?
questions.explanation: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) was developed by NPCI to facilitate instant mobile transactions directly between bank accounts using QR codes.

questions.question: The difference between the higher interest rate charged on loans and the lower interest rate paid on customer deposits is called the interest _____.
questions.explanation: Interest spread (lending rate minus deposit rate) covers bank operational costs and constitutes its principal profit margin.

questions.question: True or False: A Current Account pays a higher annual interest rate to depositors than a Fixed Deposit (FD).
questions.explanation: A Current Account pays zero interest because it is designed for unlimited daily business transactions. Fixed Deposits lock funds for a set term and pay the highest interest rate.

questions.question: Explain how financial intermediation works in commercial banking.
questions.correct_answer: Commercial banks act as financial intermediaries. They collect surplus money from depositors (savers) who want to keep cash safe and earn interest. The bank pools these funds and lends them as credit/loans to borrowers (entrepreneurs, farmers, home buyers) who pay lending interest.
questions.explanation: This mechanism channels idle household savings into productive economic investments across the country.

questions.question: Calculate and compare the returns on a ₹10,000 deposit over 3 years at 10% annual interest under Simple Interest (SI) versus Compound Interest (CI).
questions.correct_answer: Simple Interest: Year 1 = ₹1000, Year 2 = ₹1000, Year 3 = ₹1000. Total Interest = ₹3,000 (Final Amount = ₹13,000). Compound Interest: Year 1 = 10% of ₹10,000 = ₹1,000 (New P = ₹11,000); Year 2 = 10% of ₹11,000 = ₹1,100 (New P = ₹12,100); Year 3 = 10% of ₹12,100 = ₹1,210. Total Interest = ₹3,310 (Final Amount = ₹13,310). CI yields ₹310 more.
questions.explanation: Compounding calculates interest on accumulated interest from prior years, generating exponential growth.

questions.question: Scenario: An artisan needs a loan of ₹50,000 to buy equipment. An informal moneylender offers cash instantly with no paperwork at 36% simple interest per year. A commercial bank offers a loan at 10% interest per year but requires identity documents (KYC). Evaluate which option the artisan should choose.
questions.correct_answer: The artisan should choose the commercial bank loan. Under the bank loan, annual interest is ₹5,000 (10%), whereas the moneylender charges ₹18,000 (36%). Unregulated moneylenders lead borrowers into severe debt traps and lack RBI legal protections, making the formal bank loan far safer despite the initial paperwork.
questions.explanation: Formal banking credit protects borrowers from extortionate interest rates and debt cycles.

questions.question: Give reasons why the ancient Chessboard Wheat Grain Legend is used to illustrate the 'magic' and danger of compounding in finance.
questions.correct_answer: In the legend, placing 1 grain on square 1 and doubling it on each square required 2^64 - 1 grains by square 64 (18.44 quintillion grains), exceeding world grain stocks. In finance, this doubling effect shows how compound interest builds wealth exponentially for patient long-term savers, but can also destroy borrowers if high-interest debts are left unpaid to double.
questions.explanation: The story visually proves that human intuition underestimates exponential growth compared to linear additions.
